messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU queue growth detected in us-west2-prod. 90th pct latency for /generate > 5s and queue length > 1200. Auto-scaling triggered but failed to provision new nodes. Paging oncall: @jamie :rotating_light:

jamie: I'm on it, grabbing metrics now. any affected customers called out?

alex: I just saw increased 429s from the hosted API dashboard, several CIDs with steady errors. Link: https://console.redwood/alerts/2105001111

priya: We have a couple of Dedicated customers reporting degraded throughput, and one large job stuck in the GPU queue (job-id: b3f9).

jamie: Checking autoscaler logs and node quota. running: 
```
kubectl -n rwd get hpa,clusterautoscaler --show-events
kubectl -n rwd logs deploy/autoscaler -f | tail -n 200
```

mike: FYI quota for GPU instances in us-west2 shows "limit reached" for preemptible gpus: current 80 / limit 80.

jamie: autoscaler is retrying but cloud provider returns 403 quota error. Looks like spot pool count hit limit. Need fallback capacity or reduce target.

ops-bot: NOTE: fallback policy attempted -> start-fallback-queue (use-dedicated) but returned 503 for first 3 attempts.

jamie: Oof. Can we ramp dedicated pool? @alex do we have reserved spare dedicated capacity in us-west2?

alex: Dedicated pools are consumed ~90%. There is a small standby pool but it's configured for non-preemptible only and needs manual approval to reassign. I can try reassigning but will take ~8-12m to spin up VMs and attach to the runtime.

priya: Customer impact: API errors and high latency to both hosted and Dedicated endpoints for certain models. Escalate to support to notify top customers?

jamie: Yes, @sarah please coordinate comms. Summary: spot preemptions and quota exhaustion caused autoscaler to fail; fallback routing partially failed causing queue growth and 429s. ETA mitigation path: 1) temporarily lower model concurrency for heavy models (reduce new requests), 2) move some traffic to smaller model variants, 3) attempt manual b2b on standby dedicated pool, 4) open cloud quota support case.

sarah: On it. I'll ping affected accounts and post status page update.

mike: Starting immediate mitigation: kicking off a canary config change to reduce default concurrency from 32->16 for model family redwood-dense-large in prod. Command: 
```
redwoodctl routes update --model redwood-dense-large --concurrency 16 --env prod
```

jamie: Good. Also enabling prefix-KV cache temporarily for common prompts to reduce token compute. Patch applied.

ops-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: redwood-dense-large concurrency set to 16 by mike at 21:05UTC. Notice: We will monitor latency and error rates for 10m.

jamie: Monitoring metrics. Queue length dropped from 1.2k -> 680 in 6m. 429s reduced but still present. Some backlog still processing.

alex: Standby dedicated pool reassign in progress, provisioning VMs now (estimated 9m). Logs show instance boot and runtime attach in progress.

jamie: Good. Also opening a quota increase request to cloud provider and filing a post-incident action: we need automated fallback to non-preemptible pool when spot requests hit quota, and improved autoscaler error handling for quota 4xx responses.

priya: Noted for followup. For tonight, can we also enable temporary soft-eviction of very long-running jobs >6h to free slots? That will help backlog.

jamie: Agree, issuing eviction policy change for batch jobs >6h in queue. Command: 
```
redwoodctl jobs evict --age 6h --env prod --reason "incident mitigation"
```

ops-bot: JOB ACTION: evict issued for 42 jobs older than 6h.

jamie: After evictions and dedicated pool attach, queue down to 120 and error rate near baseline. Customers started recovering.

sarah: Sent status update to affected customers and posted incident note on status.redwood.ai.

jamie: Closing the active page. Followups: (1) automatic fallback to non-preemptible pools on quota 4xx, (2) autoscaler should surface quota errors to oncall faster, (3) add alert for sustained autoscaler 4xx failures, (4) increase regional GPU quota requests for us-west2. I'll create a ticket and assign owners.

alex: Created ticket INF-4271 with proposed remediation and owners.

jamie: Thanks all. If anything regresses ping here and re-open page. :thumbsup:
